A '''projective cone''' (or just '''cone''') in [[projective geometry]] is the [[Union (set theory)|union]] of all [[Line (geometry)|lines]] that [[Intersection|intersect]] a [[Projective space|projective subspace]]<ref>{{cite web |title=Projective geometry - Conic Sections, Duality, Invariance {{!}} Britannica |url=https://www.britannica.com/science/projective-geometry/Projective-conic-sections |website=britannica.com |access-date=14 August 2026 |language=en}}</ref> ''R'' (the apex of the cone) and an arbitrary [[subset]] ''A'' (the [[Basis (linear algebra)|basis]]) of some other [[Space (mathematics)|subspace]] ''S'', [[Disjoint sets|disjoint]] from ''R''.  

In the special case that ''R'' is a single [[Point (geometry)|point]], ''S'' is a [[Plane (mathematics)|plane]], and ''A'' is a [[conic section]] on ''S'', the projective cone is a [[conical surface]]; hence the name.

==Definition==

Let ''X'' be a projective space over some field ''K'', and ''R'', ''S'' be disjoint subspaces of ''X''.  Let ''A'' be an arbitrary subset of ''S''. Then we define ''RA'', the cone with top ''R'' and basis ''A'', as follows :
* When ''A'' is empty, ''RA'' = ''A''.
* When ''A'' is not empty, ''RA'' consists of all those [[point (geometry)|points]] on a line connecting a point on ''R'' and a point on ''A''.

==Properties==

* As ''R'' and ''S'' are disjoint, one may deduce from [[linear algebra]] and the definition of a projective space that every point on ''RA'' not in ''R'' or ''A'' is on exactly one line connecting a point in ''R'' and a point in ''A''.
* (''RA'') <math>\cap</math> ''S'' = ''A''
* When ''K'' is the [[finite field]] of order ''q'', then <math>|R A|</math> = <math>q^{r+1}</math><math>|A|</math> + <math>\frac{q^{r+1}-1}{q-1}</math>, where ''r'' = dim(''R'').
